one_month_reasoning: The only material scheduled event is Q3 2026 earnings, and its date is still unconfirmed. I re-searched on 2026-10-05 and found no Reddit 8-K or IR release. TipRanks lists Wed 4 Nov after the close as 'confirmed'. MarketBeat says Reddit has not confirmed and estimates Thu 29 Oct. Reddit has reported on the Thursday at month end for the last four quarters (Q3'25 30 Oct, Q1'26 30 Apr, Q2'26 30 Jul). A release after the close on 4 Nov would fall outside the window, because the 4 Nov close comes first. I lower my in-window probability from 60% to 55%: the supervisor's view, which I checked and agree with, because the TipRanks label is the one piece of contrary evidence. I modelled a mixture centred on spot: a 13% one-month sigma without the event, plus a 17% earnings-jump sigma in the 55% branch. There is no directional edge. The $860-870M guide looks beatable (Q1 and Q2 beat the top of guidance by about 10-11%), but the stock trades on traffic and users. Q3 is the first quarter without the logged-in/out split, and the -21% reaction to Q2 came despite a beat and a raise. Alt-data traffic signals (Similarweb) lean slightly negative but are single-panel estimates, so they do not tilt the ladder. P(>= $151.69) = 0.50.

fair_value.method: Blend at the 12-month horizon: 65% P/E, which applies the consistent-basis peer median of 17.6x to taxed NTM adjusted EPS at Oct 2027 of $9.09 to give $160; and 35% DCF (SBC-burdened, taxed FCF; 11% WACC; 3.5% terminal growth) at $181. Result: $167. This replaces round 1's $164; the EV/EBITDA leg is dropped because it rested on one peer.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) adjusted EPS untaxed $11.51 = 0.25 x CY27 $9.69 + 0.75 x CY28 $12.11; taxed at 21% = $9.09; x 17.6x peer median = $160

inputs_detail.input: CY2027 adjusted EPS consensus (StockAnalysis non-GAAP, SBC added back, almost untaxed)

inputs_detail.derivation: $9.69 x 1.25. Street CY2028 revenue is about $5.5B (+23%) on CY2027's $4.46B, with modest margin expansion. That is the same growth I used in round 1 for GAAP EPS (+26%), trimmed slightly.

Q2'26 pretax income was about $257M and net income $253M, so tax was about 1.5% because of the full US valuation allowance (supervisor finding, checked against the press release). Peers' consensus EPS is fully taxed, so for like-for-like I apply a 21% book rate. The 10-Q says a valuation-allowance release is reasonably possible within 12 months. NOLs keep cash tax low for a few years, which is a modest upside (a few $/share) that I leave unquantified for lack of a disclosed NOL balance. Note: 9.69 x 0.79 = $7.66 for CY27, lower than the supervisor's about $8.2.

The median of 11 peers on one basis: StockAnalysis CY2027 non-GAAP EPS, all December fiscal years, prices 2026-10-05, SPOT converted from EUR at 1.17. Range 7.3-38.7x. I apply the median with no premium (see comps_summary).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue $4.46B (2027), $5.5B (2028), then growth of 20/17/14/11/8% to $10.6B in 2033. SBC-burdened, taxed FCF margin 24% (2027) rising to 30% from 2030. WACC 11%, terminal growth 3.5%. EV at horizon $34.0B + $3.5B net cash, / 207M diluted shares = $181

inputs_detail.derivation: A fade from about 23% in 2028 toward GDP-plus. The fade is steeper than the street because traffic depends on Google (57% organic search per Similarweb, a single-panel estimate; the 10-Q confirms search-algorithm effects on DAUq).

inputs_detail.input: FCF margin after SBC and tax
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2'26 adjusted EBITDA margin 42.6%, with Q3 guided to about 45%; FCF of $261M is about 32% of revenue before SBC and almost untaxed. Taking a long-run adjusted EBITDA of about 48-50%, less SBC of about 10% of revenue, less D&A, then taxed at 21%, gives about 30%.
A high-beta single-platform name (70% realized vol, traffic concentration risk), so a premium over a large-cap internet WACC of about 9%.
$2.79B at Q2'26 with no debt, plus about $1.1-1.3B of FCF over 5 quarters, less buybacks of about $235M a quarter. The supervisor's $3.5B matches my arithmetic.

bear.story: AI search keeps eroding logged-out referral traffic, US DAUq declines year on year, and the Google licence (only $30.1M of 2027 RPO contracted) lapses or reprices, hurting sentiment more than revenue. 2027 revenue growth slows to about 20%, taxed NTM adjusted EPS at the horizon is about $7.0, and the stock trades at about 14x, the lower half of the peer range.

base.story: Revenue grows about 30% in 2027 on ARPU and international gains while US traffic stays choppy, and licensing renews at about flat terms. Taxed NTM EPS of about $9.1 at about the peer median of 17.6x, cross-checked by the DCF at $181.

bull.story: Beats continue at the round-1 pace (10%+ over guidance), search traffic stabilizes, international logged-out users convert, and licensing renews at higher terms. Taxed NTM EPS of about $10.5 at about 22x, an upper-quartile peer multiple the market would pay if 25%+ growth proves durable.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E 7.3x (SNAP) to 38.7x (ROKU), median 17.6x across 11 peers; interquartile range about 8.9-23.0x. Basis: StockAnalysis CY2027 non-GAAP consensus EPS, all December fiscal years, prices 2026-10-05, SPOT's EUR EPS converted at 1.17 (round 1 left it unconverted at 31.3x; corrected to 26.7x). StockAnalysis's 'Forward PE' field mixes fiscal years, so I did not use it. Peer forward EV/EBITDA could not be sourced consistently (StockAnalysis gives only trailing figures, e.g. META 17.5x), so no EV/EBITDA median is reported and that method is dropped. WB (4.6x, China discount, +8% growth) and YELP (3% growth) were excluded as not comparable.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17.6x taxed NTM adjusted EPS at the horizon: exactly the median, no premium. On the same basis RDDT trades today at 15.7x untaxed CY27 adjusted EPS ($151.69/$9.69), or 19.8x once that EPS is taxed at 21% ($7.66). The supervisor's 18.5x assumes about $8.2 taxed, which I could not reproduce at a 21% rate. So on a like-for-like tax basis RDDT already trades about 12% above the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: None applied. Reddit's growth is structurally higher (CY27 revenue +32% against a peer median of about 13%), but its persistence through Oct 2027 is not established. Traffic depends on Google: the 10-Q cites search-algorithm effects on DAUq, US DAUq is flat QoQ, and a class action concerns AI Overviews. The Google licence renewal has only $30.1M contracted for 2027. My alt-data reads point the same way (Similarweb's 57% organic share and Sistrix volatility, both single-panel estimates). Higher growth is captured in the earnings path (CY28 EPS +25%), not in the multiple, so applying a premium as well would double-count it.

thesis_break_reason: $108 is about 9% below the 52-week low of $119.27 and about 14x taxed CY27 adjusted EPS ($7.66), which is about 12x my taxed NTM EPS at the horizon. That is bottom-third peer multiples for a company still growing 30%+. A price there would most likely mean the market expects structural traffic loss: total DAUq falling year on year, guidance implying sub-20% growth, or Google cutting off or repricing access with a visible hit to search referrals. Ordinary 70%-vol noise would not explain it.

Monthly Similarweb and Sistrix traffic prints; any Google core update affecting Reddit's ranking
Google AI data-licensing renewal (only $30.1M of licensing RPO contracted for 2027); outcomes from cutoff to repricing

The Google licence renewal in 1H27: small for revenue ($30.1M contracted for 2027) but large for the traffic relationship and sentiment
Flat US DAUq (53.2M, +6% YoY, flat QoQ) set against strong international growth
The tax basis: consensus EPS is almost untaxed; the timing of the valuation-allowance release and the NOL value are unquantified
The Q3 earnings date, and therefore whether the reaction falls in the 1-month window
reasoning: Round 2 corrects the factual and basis errors the supervisor flagged. (1) Tax basis: Q2'26 net income of $253M on about $257M pretax confirms consensus EPS is almost untaxed, so I now tax EPS at 21% before applying peer multiples. That cuts my P/E-leg EPS by about a fifth, offset by moving to adjusted EPS (SBC added back), which is the basis peers' consensus uses. (2) Comps: SPOT is corrected to 26.7x, and I added MTCH and ROKU (both verified on StockAnalysis) to reach 11 peers on one CY27 non-GAAP basis. The median is unchanged at 17.6x. I verified META 21.3x and SPOT myself. (3) EV/EBITDA is dropped (one peer, and no consistent forward data) and replaced by a DCF with an explicit SBC charge and tax. (4) The Forbes ChatGPT-citation snippet and the Wells Fargo $550M scenario are removed from the numbers; the bull case now rests on beats and traffic stabilization, not on $550M of licensing. The P/E leg gives $160 and the DCF $181; blended 65/35 the fair value is $167. I disagree slightly with the supervisor's $8.2 taxed CY27 adjusted EPS: 21% tax on $9.69 gives $7.66, which makes RDDT look about 12% rich against peers today, not in line. Scenarios: $100 / $167 / $235 at 25/50/25%. The mean is $167.25, which reconciles with fair value: the bear and bull legs are set roughly symmetric in dollar terms around fair value. Each is modelled as a lognormal (sigma 0.33 / 0.28 / 0.30), giving a median of about $157, below the mean because of right skew. P(>= spot) is 0.535, a modest positive drift consistent with fair value 10% above spot but tempered by traffic risk and 70% realized vol. The ladder is close to round 1, slightly thinner in the upper tail (the bull leg is $235, not $250). The 1-month ladder stays symmetric, with 55% weight on an earnings jump inside the window. Research was limited to about 8 follow-up fetches/searches.
